title: Ask draws a dog, or a smiley face icon, you can tell at a glance
goal: When a person asks for a drawing (a dog, a house, a coffee cup), Ask makes a clean, recognizable picture out of editable shapes, the kind a person would be happy to show. Today it stacks straight-edged brown shards that nobody would call a dog.
notes:
The user, 2026-10-20 07:35, Ask on a blank picture: 'draw a picture of a dog.' Plan ran 9 steps: add_path Dog Body, Dog Head, Dog Snout, Dog Ear x2, Dog Leg x2, Dog Snout again, add_text "Dog". Result: one brown angular blob with spiky triangles off it and the word Dog above. User: 'this is so embarrassing. what can we do to improve the drawing capabilities'.

Why it is bad (suspects, check them first):
- The default Ask model is qwen3:30b (Ollama), which is TEXT ONLY, so it plans every coordinate blind and never sees the result. gemma-4-31B on this Mac (ollama list) can take a picture; see what Ollama on this Mac offers that can see.
- add_path supports smooth points and handles (Sources/PhotonzCore/AgentTools.swift:283) but the model used only corners. A small model is poor at writing many separate coordinate calls; models are much better at writing ONE SVG for the whole drawing.
- AskPlanning.swift builds the prompt (:426); there is no draw, look, revise loop.

Ways in, the runner picks and logs why (do not stop to ask):
1. Let Ask write one SVG for a drawing and bring it in as editable layers. That needs SVG to come in as layers: queue task opening-an-svg-file-gives-you-its-drawing-to-edi is pending at p2, and this task can do the importing part it needs.
2. A draw, look, revise loop with a model that can see (on this Mac, offline).
3. A built-in set of simple drawings (an openly licensed illustration or icon set, licence checked and recorded) Ask can place and restyle when it is asked for a common thing, drawing from scratch only otherwise.
4. Some mix of these. Measure, do not assume: the blind naming score decides.

The Claude Code route (MCP plus skill) drew the box in a cloud icon well yesterday (queue/audits/2026-10-19-agent-skill-2-icon-rendered.png); that is the bar for what these tools can make when the model is strong. App copy never names Claude or Anthropic.

Score with the eval (a-scored-test-set-for-what-ask-and-the-photonz-s): its drawing cases are this task's twelve. Climb: keep a change only when the score goes up. The user's screenshot: queue/audits/2026-10-20-user-ask-dog.png.

Second report, 2026-10-20 07:44, 'create a smiley face icon': plan add_shape Smiley Face, Left Eye, Right Eye. The yellow circle sits at about (520,420) 190 wide, both eyes ABOVE it at y about 390, no mouth at all, on a 1440x1024 picture. User: 'gross. this isn't an icon, the eyes aren't in the face, there is no smile'. Same blind-coordinates cause. A cheap rule the builder can run without a model that sees: parts named for a whole (eye, mouth, ear) must lie inside or touch that whole, and every part a thing needs (a face: two eyes and a mouth) must be in the plan.
acceptance: MEASURED BAR, run in the audit: thirteen requests on a blank picture at Next defaults (a dog, a smiley face icon, a cat, a house, a tree, a car, a bicycle, a coffee cup, a fish, a bird, a rocket, a flower, the sun over mountains). Each render is shown, with no hint, to a model that can see and did not draw it, which is asked what it shows. At least 11 of 13 must be named correctly. Today's dog fails this; the audit runs today's build first and records its score as the before

Parts sit where they belong, checked from the read document: for a face, the eyes and the smile are inside the head; for an animal, ears, legs and snout touch the body. The user's smiley (queue/audits/2026-10-20-user-ask-smiley-icon.png: eyes floating above the circle, no smile) is a case and must pass
A request for an icon makes an icon: a square icon-sized picture (the app's icon setup, epic icon-svg), the drawing centred on its keylines and filling them, and it exports as clean SVG
Drawings use curves and ovals where the thing is round (a dog's head, ears, body), not only straight corners, and every part stays an editable, named layer that one Command Z removes

Ask looks at what it drew before it hands back: it renders the result, a model that can see judges it, and it revises at most twice. If it still cannot make the thing, it says so in one short plain sentence instead of leaving a mess
Runs on this Mac with networking off, and the time from Ask to the finished drawing is measured (median of five) and in the audit

Audit under queue/audits/ with a contact sheet of all twelve before and after, the blind naming results and the times. Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not

eval landed (a-scored-test-set-for-what-ask-and-the-photonz-s): Scripts/ask-eval.sh run --engine ask --cases dog,smiley-icon,cat,house,tree,car,bicycle,coffee-cup,fish,bird,rocket,flower,sun-over-mountains --tag '<change>' then compare. Ask baseline 2026-10-20 (run 20261020-165619-ask): drawings 35.4/100, named right blind 1 of 13 (car; dog read as bear, house as suitcase, rocket as mailbox, cat as teddy bear; fish and tree wrote their own names). Skill baseline 87.2, 13 of 13 named. Two Ask drawings (cat, sun over mountains) placed a starter Card component inside the drawing.

Measured before choosing (2026-10-20 runner): qwen3:30b asked for ONE whole SVG per subject (not many add_path calls) drew smiley, house, tree, car, bird, sun over mountains recognizably; dog and cat read as a mouse, cup as a jar, bicycle as a box. Twemoji (graphics CC-BY 4.0) has all 13 cleanly; llama3.2-vision:latest (on this Mac, 6s a look) named all 13 Twemoji renders right and caught qwen's dog and cat as 'mouse'. Chose a mix (way 4): a built-in drawing set from Twemoji first, a whole model-written SVG when the set has no match, and a look-and-revise step with llama3.2-vision, over SVG-only because SVG-only still fails the animals and the bicycle blind; over a library-only because a library alone cannot draw anything it lacks. gemma-4-31B here has no vision projector (ollama show: completion, tools, thinking).

intake 2026-10-20 11:35: the user ran sun over mountains and called flat triangles bad (queue/audits/2026-10-20-user-ask-sun-over-mountains.png). Illustration craft (natural ridges, light and shadow, depth) is its own task right after this one, an-illustration-ask-draws-looks-illustrated-natu; do not widen this task for it, but do not pick a route that makes it impossible (for example only flat emoji art for every request).

Adversarial review before building: a first-time user types 'draw a dog' and expects a dog they would show someone, not a set of shapes to fix; a Photoshop user would expect a placed, editable vector (like a library shape or a pasted SVG), grouped and undoable in one step, which is what add_drawing makes. What the old route could not deliver: a text-only model placing shapes blind (smiley eyes above the head). Risk: a built-in set looks like emoji; accepted because the user's bar is 'recognizable at a glance' and every part stays editable, and it is in the audit's evaluate list.

Chose the built-in drawing over the model's own SVG when both exist (builtIn true by default) because the set's drawings are vetted and the model's are the weak part; the model can still ask for its own with builtIn false. Chose to name only face parts automatically (FaceParts, from position) over naming every part because nothing names a dog's ear without a model; faces are what the checklist checks. Chose 'I couldn't make a clear drawing of that. Nothing was changed.' over leaving the last try, per the checklist.

Pictures looked at: queue/audits/2026-10-20-ask-drawings-before-after.png (13 pairs: before a bear-shaped block, a suitcase house, a sword rocket; after the Twemoji dog, cat, house, tree, car, bicycle, cup, fish, bird, rocket, daisy, sunrise over mountains, smiley), 1-dog-sc.png (Dog group of 12 parts picked over the blank canvas, Agent row 'Drew a drawing'), 3-smiley-icon-sc.png (512 x 512 icon frame with keylines, face on the circle keyline, previews 16 to 64). Exported SVG of the icon: ellipses plus one path, no bitmap.

left rough (no task: small, folded or by design): the Agent row says 'Drew a drawing' not the thing; built-in non-face parts are numbered (Dog 1..12); the coffee cup's third blind look said 'hot coffee', which the case's names (cup, mug, teacup) do not take; first look after idle costs ~12 s while llama3.2-vision loads; the eval history briefly held two trial runs of mine (3 and 3 cases), which I removed so they do not stand as the best.

Ask draws a thing in one add_drawing call: a built-in set of 992 Twemoji drawings (CC-BY 4.0, credited in Open Source Notices) or the model's own SVG, read into one named group of editable layers (SVGArtwork); icon on a blank picture becomes a 512 pt icon frame on its keylines; Ask looks with llama3.2-vision and redraws at most twice or says it could not. Eval 13 drawing cases: 35.4 -> 92, named blind 1 -> 13 of 13, median 18.4 s. Verified: 14052 tests green, ask-draws-a-dog-walk ok at Next defaults (one Command Z removes the dog; smiley icon 512x512 with eyes and mouth inside the face), icon exports as clean SVG.
